subject: Private deployment – egress, peering & network checks for tail-latency SLO

Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 16:12:00 -0700
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
To: Alice Cho <alice.cho@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>
Subject: Follow-up: private deployment network/egress details for latency SLO

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can scope the Private deployment preflight:

Recap (what we heard)
- Target SLO: p99 tail latency for streaming requests to be <= 120 ms end-to-end (application -> model first-byte / steady-state token).
- Peak traffic: estimated 40 concurrent streams during business hours, ~350 peak requests/minute (burst to ~80 concurrent for short periods).
- Token throughput target (for load tests): ~6k tokens/sec across the cluster during peak.
- Deployment: customer-managed VPC in us-west-2 with Direct Connect/Transit Gateway.
- Egress constraints: all outbound calls must be restricted to specific Redwood IP ranges; outbound NAT via central egress (no public internet routes from compute subnets).

Asks / info we need from your side to progress:
1) Network path – confirm whether you want (a) Direct Connect + Transit Gateway peering, or (b) VPN over public internet for the initial preflight. If Direct Connect, please share the DX location and peering contact.
2) Allowed egress IPs – we'll provide a short list; we need the CIDR(s) you will permit on your side.
3) Internal latency budget – we need app -> private-runtime RTT target inside your VPC. Can you confirm average and 95th that your app tier expects? We usually ask for <20 ms RTT to hit the requested p99 end-to-end.
4) MTU, TCP proxy or TLS termination – are you terminating TLS at a load balancer? Any AWS NLB/ALB in front of traffic to Redwood components?
5) Test access – a temporary SRE account (or jumpbox IP) for iperf/iperf3 and traceroute tests to validate path and to establish baseline.

Proposed Redwood plan
- Provide IP ranges and preflight runbook (attached: MVP-network-checklist.pdf).
- Redwood to spin a staging Private environment in us-west-2 that mirrors the production topology for a 72-hour soak.
- Coordinate a 2-hour test window where we run streaming load (token-level harness) and share p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and per-token latency.

Next steps
- Can you confirm items 1–4 above by Tue, Apr 20?
- If Direct Connect, please loop in your peering contact so we can coordinate provisioning lead time.
- Proposed test window: Thurs Apr 22 10:00–12:00 PT — OK on your side?

Attaching: MVP-network-checklist.pdf for your network team.

Happy to hop on a quick 20m call with your SRE if that speeds things up.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodai.com | +1 (415) 555-0126

Subject: Re: Follow-up: private deployment network/egress details for latency SLO

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline: 

1) Network path: we plan to use AWS Direct Connect (DX) through our Transit Gateway. Provisioning is already in flight for us-west-2 (DX location: Equinix SV4). I'll loop in our peering contact (Chris Lee) separately.

2) Allowed egress IPs: please send the list. We will only permit the ranges you provide on a CIDR allowlist for egress.

3) Internal latency budget: our app tier SLA target is 30 ms average RTT east-west and p95 < 60 ms inside the VPC. Our team is comfortable with Redwood aiming to keep service RTT < 20 ms to meet the end-to-end p99 target you outlined.

4) TLS termination: we terminate TLS at an internal NLB; we use TCP passthrough to the application. No proxy rewriting. MTU is standard 9001 across our DX connections.

Test access: we can open a temporary jumpbox (10.12.5.18) with SSH for you. Chris (SRE) will run iperf/iperf3 on the target and will coordinate exact commands.

A couple notes: we will also require that any outbound connections from the Redwood runtime respect our egress logging and that you provide a short list of expected FQDNs for TLS SNI-based inspection.

Scheduling: Apr 22 window works. Please send the IP ranges and runbook by EOD Mon (Apr 20) so Chris can pre-approve firewall rules.

Alice
Alice Cho

Alice —

Great, thanks for the details — that's exactly the level of info we need. Quick responses and plan from Redwood side: 

1) IP ranges: attaching a short list of outbound CIDRs we require for the preflight (see attached redwood-preflight-runbook.md). For the test window we'll only use the small sandbox subset (3 /24 ranges).

2) Egress logging & SNI: we will provide the expected FQDNs and also a temporary TLS cert fingerprint list for your inspection. We can also present HTTP(S) target IPs if that helps your DPI team.

3) Test plan & tooling: Ben (copied) will run the streaming harness: it opens N concurrent WebSocket streams and pushes tokenized payloads to simulate real client sessions. Expected metrics we will report: first-byte latency, per-token latency distribution, throughput (tokens/sec), and error rate. We'll also run iperf3 before and after to establish baseline network capacity.

4) Preflight environment: Redwood will stand up a staging Private cluster in us-west-2 with identical instance sizing to the production plan and keep it available for the 72-hour soak. During the test window we will run 2–3 ramp profiles (5m warmup, 20m run, 10m cooldown).

Action items for Acme SRE (by EOD Mon Apr 20):
- Confirm jumpbox ssh is reachable from our test IPs (we'll provide IPs).
- Open temporary firewall entries for Redwood sandbox CIDRs.
- Share contact for Direct Connect peering (Chris Lee).

Scheduling: we propose Thu Apr 22 10:00–12:00 PT. If Chris wants a pre-check on Wed Apr 21 10:00 PT, Ben can be available to run iperf3.

Ben / Dev — can you own the test harness and the preflight runbook respectively? I've attached our runbook and the small CIDR list.

Thanks,
Jonas
